data.name: BuildBackendAnswered
data.value: Embeddings came back after {0}s. Embedding continues.
data.comment: RoslynRestored's shape and its rule: printed only where the wait ended in an answer, so a run that shows the waiting line, then a stop, and no answered line is telling the truth. It says the embeddings came back and not that Ollama answered, for the reason BuildBackendWaiting no longer names Ollama either: on the commonest outage Ollama answered every request all the way through, with an HTTP 400 whose body named a runner it could not reach, and on the broker_start_timeout route what came back was the broker. What is checked here is that this call returned vectors, so that is what the line states. Seconds rather than the waiting line's minutes, for the same reason RoslynRestored takes seconds where RoslynLoading takes minutes: one figure is a budget and the other is measured, and this one is subtracted from SyncFinished's own seconds. It measures the whole outage from the moment the patient path was entered, not the last attempt. Deliberately not one total at the end of the build: a total over concurrent waiters is a wall clock rather than a sum of their waits, and a breakdown printed once the run is over is what SyncFinished's own comment already refuses.

data.name: BuildBackendWaiting
data.value: The build is waiting — up to {0} min.
data.comment: Said before the wait, not after it - RoslynLoading's rule, for the same reason: a line printed once the wait is over explains a silence the reader has already sat through. It names no cause, and that is the change: the clause it used to open with was EmbeddingBackendUnavailable's own, copied on the ground that it was the same state, and it is not one state but seven. Counted rather than guessed - one build on this machine hit runner_unreachable 25 times in 28 minutes and an unreachable endpoint not once, while this line said Ollama was not available and Ollama was answering throughout. The cause now stands on BuildBackendStalled, once, in the words of whatever refused. What is left is one hole, and it counts down: the figure that changes from line to line is what tells a reader the build is alive, and a second changing number in a line that prints a dozen times in a row is noise - not the attempt number, and not the chunk count, which BuildEmbedded printed above. Minutes, F1 and invariant. Nothing here says stopped or failed: this wait is handled, and BuildEmbeddingStopped is the end. Printed from one place: the builder posts the next batch before awaiting the current one, so two batches are in flight when the backend goes away, and two unserialised waiters would print two countdowns of one outage. The Russian is unchanged to the byte - it never carried the false clause in its second sentence, and the English now matches its shape rather than the other way round.

data.name: EmbeddingBrokerNotStarted
data.value: The LocalAi broker did not start in time. {0}
data.comment: {0} is BrokerBootstrapException's own diagnostic - phase and last observation - which is English in every language because BrokerProcess has no catalogue of its own. It restates this sentence in English, and that duplication goes away when those messages are catalogued rather than by dropping this one: dropping it is the defect #393 names.

data.name: EmbeddingBackendUnavailable
data.value: The embedding job for model '{0}' did not finish. {1}
data.comment: No cause, because the catch cannot establish one. It fires on a single failure code, BackendUnavailableException, and five states arrive under it: runner_unreachable from OllamaTransport's exhausted retries, and active_model_missing, backend_unreachable, backend_http_NNN and backend_io_failure from the watchdog's probe. Only one of the five is consistent with an absent Ollama, and an Ollama that is not running never reaches this catch at all - the job never runs, and BrokerBackendUnreachableException carries its own sentence and its own action, backed by a TCP connect to the endpoint. Measured twice during one build: this line printed while ollama.exe was serving, the model held 11.7 GB of the card at 82-91% utilisation, and llama-server was listening on the very port the body reported as refusing, with 48 sockets to it in TIME_WAIT; the build waited 182.7 s and 204.1 s and resumed on its own. So the sentence states what was observed - the job did not finish - and leaves which state it was to {1}. {1} is BrokerJobFailedException's message, already catalogued and already cut to 200 characters, so the job id and the marker before the backend's own words come with it - do not re-derive them from FailureReason. No action clause either: on the patient path the countdown under this line says the build is waiting, and on the terminal path BuildEmbeddingStopped has already said that running the build again continues from where it stopped. {0} is the embedding model id and is never translated.

data.name: EmbeddingModelMissing

data.comment: Says only what was checked: Ollama answered /api/embed with 404 and /api/tags does not list the model. The second sentence points where to look without claiming it as the cause. Always followed by one of the EmbeddingModelInstall* sentences.

data.value: Otherwise install it through the broker: localai-launcher.exe run localai model pull --model {0} --catalog-version {1}
data.comment: Only when the catalog was read and names the model in its maintenance allowlist; otherwise the broker refuses the pull. No full stop: the line ends in a command somebody copies.

data.name: BuildEmbeddingStopped
data.value: Embedding stopped at {0} of {1} chunks. What is embedded is saved — running this build again continues from there.
data.comment: The count is what #389 was filed for, and the second clause is the fact that makes running it again cheap. Both holes are counts and stay invariant. Said only where an embedding checkpoint is configured, and understated by construction: SaveBatch runs before done is incremented, and the halving path saves more, so what the checkpoint holds is never less than what this claims.

data.name: BuildEmbeddingStoppedAtStart
data.value: None of the {0} chunks were embedded.
data.comment: No remedy clause: nothing was finished, so there is nothing to tell the reader is kept.

data.name: BuildTooManyChunks
data.value: This build comes to {0} chunks, and one index holds at most {1} at {2} dimensions. No embedding was started, and another run would stop in the same place.
data.comment: Refused before any embedding, which is the whole of #397: the same arithmetic used to fail inside Assemble as an OutOfMemoryException from new float[(long)totalChunks * dim], after every chunk had already been embedded. All three holes are counts and stay invariant. {0} is the chunk total the finished index would hold - fresh plus reused, the same tally Assemble makes - not BuildChunked's count of what is left to embed: on an incremental build the two differ by orders of magnitude, and the smaller one printed beside the ceiling reads as a limit that was not reached. {1} is Array.MaxLength / {2}, computed rather than written down, so the sentence cannot drift from the limit it describes. It is an upper bound and nothing else: a build well under it can still exhaust the machine, which is why the line says at most and promises nothing below it. The dimension is carried because it is what makes the ceiling a quotient rather than a product constant - another embedding model gives another ceiling for the same tree, and this is the figure that says why. No colon anywhere: what stands left of the first colon is a field name and stays English, and this sentence is translated whole. No remedy clause, and deliberately - nothing this product offers moves any of the three things that would help. localai sync takes --root, --base-only, --require-semantics and --max-inline-files and no path filter; FileScanner's exclusions are a fixed list plus git ls-files --exclude-standard; and the embedding model comes from the routing catalogue rather than from localai policy set. Naming any of them would name a route the reader cannot take. What stands in the remedy's place is the one thing he would otherwise do, and it is the exact negation of BuildEmbeddingStopped's second clause: that line says a repeated run continues from where it stopped, this one says it stops in the same place. That sentence also pins where the guard may stand - it is false anywhere after EmbedAsync has begun, so a later guard that waits for the first vector to learn the width needs a key of its own.

data.comment: The count is honest only after the call - MSBuildWorkspace.OpenSolutionAsync is one opaque operation with no per-project callback, so this is the first moment the number exists. Both holes are invariant.

data.name: StepStillRunning
data.value: Still running, {0}s so far.
data.comment: A time and nothing else: no fraction, no estimate, no claim about what remains, because a step with no per-item callback can compute none of those honestly. Its cadence is IndexBuilder.TargetBatchDuration, referenced rather than repeated, so nothing anywhere in a sync goes quiet for longer than one embedding batch. A step that finishes inside the interval prints this line no times at all, which is the point: its presence is always information rather than noise, and that is the property the tests pin. Seconds arrive F1 and invariant.

data.name: RoslynAnalysing
data.value: Analysed {0}/{1} projects.
data.comment: The one place in the semantic phase where a fraction is a fact rather than a guess: the project count is known before the first iteration, and it is the same figure RoslynOpened printed a moment earlier, so 7/26 closes against a number the reader has already seen. Printed after the project it counts, not before it - 1/26 before the work is a promise. Throttled by elapsed time rather than by every Nth project, because a per-N rule is wrong at both ends; a fast analysis therefore prints this line no times at all, which is why RoslynAnalysed prints unconditionally. Both holes are counts and stay invariant. Analysed is разобрано in Russian - the register of Открыто, Просмотрено and Сохранено beside it - and RoslynAnalysed uses the same verb, because it is the same action.

data.name: RoslynAnalysed
data.value: Analysed {0} projects and {1} files in {2}s.
data.comment: Printed whether or not RoslynAnalysing ever was: this is the only line that ever states how many files the C# analysis took in, and a closing line that appears only on slow machines makes two runs incomparable. The file count is documents.Count - repository-relative source files that produced a semantic model, bin and obj excluded - not BuildScanned's, which counts every indexable file in the tree by extension. The project count repeats RoslynOpened's deliberately: it closes RoslynAnalysing's {0}/{1} and lets the line stand alone, and it can never be the smaller number, since the loop covers every project and cancellation throws before this line. No colon before the figures: what stands left of the first colon is a field name and stays English, and this sentence is translated whole. Seconds arrive F1 and invariant, as every duration here.

data.comment: One sentence for every way ReadManifest refuses - the directory gone, the manifest gone or unparseable, an identity that does not match its directory, a checksum that does not match - because none of them changes what the reader does, which is the argument SemanticIndexUnreadableFact's own comment makes and CodeSearchSyncCommand.TryReadManifest already acts on. data.name: BuildBackendStalled
data.value: No embeddings are coming back. {0}
data.comment: Printed once per outage, immediately before the first countdown line and never again while that outage lasts: the cause is worth one line and the countdown is worth a dozen. {0} is EmbeddingUnavailableException's own message, which is already the composed, catalogued, length-bounded sentence for whichever state this is - broker_start_timeout, runner_unreachable, active_model_missing, backend_unreachable, backend_http_NNN, backend_io_failure, or an endpoint answering nothing at all - so nothing here re-derives it from a code and nothing up here learns Ollama's vocabulary, which is what OllamaTransport.NamesAnUnreachableRunner's own comment argues for. Named for the build rather than for Ollama, and deliberately: on the commonest of those states Ollama is up and answering in the same 7-16 seconds a success takes, and what has gone is the runner behind it. The clause before {0} is close to a restatement of what follows it, and that is the point: {0} ends in a foreign sentence of unbounded shape, and one owned clause in the reader's own language has to stand in front of it. It says nothing about giving up, because the line under it says the opposite.

data.name: SemanticOverlayLayered
data.value: Semantic overlay: {0} files changed since the commit, {1} taken from its overlay.
data.comment: Printed once, immediately after the semantic overlay is saved, and it is how a reader tells which route the rebuild took. {0} is the saved files whose content no longer matches what the committed overlay or the base index records - the plan's own input, not every dirty file. {1} is what came across from the commit's overlay untouched, taken as the layer's document count minus the rebuild's, because the rebuild's count is not the number of files it was asked about: Roslyn opens a requested project's references along with it, and the indexer writes a document for every file in every project it ends up with. The size of the parse itself stays on RoslynAnalysed, which is the only line that states it.

data.name: SemanticOverlayFromBase

data.comment: The other route, printed for the reason the first one is: without it, the absence of the layered line cannot be told from the line not being reached. Says the base index rather than the whole solution because two routes end here - narrowed by project but measured against the base generation, and not narrowed at all - and what separates those two is already on screen in RoslynOpened's project count. No token for which of the six causes it was; none of them changes what the reader does next.
